title: Analyzing XRP’s $44M liquidation imbalance – Is a market reset underway?
summary: XRP's derivatives market is cooling after a wave of forced liquidations, but persistent ETF withdrawals could limit any price recovery.

title: Hackers inject credit card, crypto-stealing malware into 178 major websites
summary: Ledger and Coinpass were among the businesses whose websites served malware designed to steal visitors’ crypto and credit card details, according to security researchers.
content: Security researchers discovered that hackers injected credit card and cryptocurrency-stealing malware into 178 major websites. Among the affected businesses whose platforms served this malicious software to unsuspecting visitors were Ledger and Coinpass. The malware was specifically designed to capture sensitive financial and digital asset details from users browsing the compromised sites.

Ledger மற்றும் Coinpass உள்ளிட்ட நிறுவனங்களின் வலைத்தளங்கள், பார்வையாளர்களின் நிதி மற்றும் டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து விவரங்களைத் திருடும் நோக்கில் உருவாக்கப்பட்ட இந்த மால்வேரை வழங்கியுள்ளன.

title: Finmo and J.P. Morgan Payments Collaborate to Help Businesses Move and Manage Money More Efficiently Across Borders
summary:
Finmo, the treasury operating system for global businesses, today announced a collaboration with J.P. Morgan Payments to leverage the bank’s global infrastructure for cross-border payments, collections, and FX on its platform, giving Finmo’s clients the reach of a global bank alongside a clear view of their cash.
Finance teams at businesses operating in multiple markets need to know where cash sits across accounts and entities, forecast upcoming obligations, manage currency exposure, and decide when and how to pay. Those decisions are harder when payments, banking and cash data sit in separate systems.
“Global businesses need more than the ability to move money. They need to understand their financial position and make decisions about cash, currencies and payments with the right context. Our relationship with J.P. Morgan Payments strengthens the infrastructure behind these flows, while Finmo Treasury connects clients to the broader financial picture at their organisation. Until now, that combination of bank-grade infrastructure and real decision support has been out of reach for most growing businesses. This collaboration, alongside the recent launch of our Business Account, is how we change that,” said David Hanna, Co-Founder and CEO of Finmo.
“At J.P. Morgan Payments, our scale, global network and cross-border capabilities enable us to support innovative fintechs as they help businesses navigate increasingly complex treasury needs,” said Christine Tan, APAC Head of FIG Sales at J.P. Morgan Payments. “By combining these capabilities with Finmo’s technology, we can make treasury simpler and more seamless for businesses looking to expand their global footprint.”
J.P. Morgan Payments combines treasury services, trade & working capital, blockchain and tokenization, and card and merchant services capabilities to help clients pay customers or employees, in different currencies, around the world. It processes nearly US$12 trillion in payments daily, operating in over 160 countries and over 120 currencies.
What it means for businesses
Payments and collections: Collections in 40+ currencies and payouts in 120+ currencies across 160+ countries, so businesses can pay suppliers, staff and partners, and collect from customers, more predictably across borders.
Foreign exchange: Institutional-grade FX pricing and liquidity, so businesses can hold and convert currencies with confidence.
Cash visibility: Payment activity flows into Finmo Treasury, so finance teams can see cash positions, upcoming obligations and movements across all accounts, entities and currencies, and with each payment or conversion understand the impact on the company’s position.
Resilience: Bank-grade infrastructure behind Finmo’s delivery of financial services across its markets.
Bringing bank-grade infrastructure to growing businesses
The collaboration follows the recent launch of the Finmo Business Account, which brings the cash visibility, forecasting and decision tools of Finmo Treasury to Singapore businesses without a dedicated finance team. With J.P. Morgan Payments’ infrastructure supporting cross-border flows, companies at every stage now have access to the reach of a global bank together with the intelligence to decide how and when their money should move.
Businesses now move more than US$1 billion through Finmo’s platform each month. The announcement also follows the opening of Finmo’s global headquarters at Suntec City, Singapore, in September 2026. As businesses operate across more entities, currencies and markets, Finmo remains focused on connecting the infrastructure that moves money with the intelligence needed to manage it.

title: Ex-OpenAI researcher fund dumps bitcoin miners, cuts IREN 94% after portfolio slump
summary: The fund swapped its common stock in Bloom Energy, Nebius and SanDisk for call options, keeping its bet on AI power, computing and memory.
content: An investment fund founded by a former OpenAI researcher has significantly reduced its holdings in bitcoin miners, cutting its stake in IREN by 94% following a recent portfolio slump. content_ta: முன்னாள் OpenAI ஆராய்ச்சியாளரால் தொடங்கப்பட்ட ஒரு முதலீட்டு நிதி, சமீபத்திய சரிவைத் தொடர்ந்து பிட்காயின் மைனிங் நிறுவனமான IREN-ல் தனது பங்குகளை 94% வரை குறைத்துள்ளது. மேலும், இந்த நிதி Bloom Energy, Nebius மற்றும் SanDisk போன்ற நிறுவனங்களின் சாதாரண பங்குகளை கால் ஆப்ஷன்களாக மாற்றியுள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவுக்கான மின்சாரம், கம்ப்யூட்டிங் மற்றும் மெமரி துறைகளில் தனது முதலீட்டைத் தொடர்கிறது.

summary: Bitcoin (BTC) is down a further 1.0% since midnight UTC at around $64,200, with its bounce from the weekend selloff stalled and pressure building on all fronts.
content: Bitcoin remained near $64,000 as its bounce from a recent weekend selloff stalled. Despite the end of a recent exchange-traded fund outflow streak, Bitcoin dropped about 1.0% since midnight UTC to trade around $64,200. Downward pressure continues to build on the cryptocurrency across multiple fronts, keeping its price heavily constrained.

title: Solana Foundation takes majority stake in crypto data provider CoinGecko
summary: The foundation plans Solana-powered trading on CoinGecko's website, GeckoTerminal and app.
content: The Solana Foundation has acquired a majority stake in crypto data provider CoinGecko. Following the investment, the foundation plans to integrate Solana-powered trading features directly into CoinGecko's website, GeckoTerminal, and its mobile application, expanding the utility of its ecosystem within widely used crypto tracking platforms.
content_ta: க்ரிப்டோ டேட்டா வழங்குநரான CoinGecko நிறுவனத்தில் Solana Foundation பெரும்பான்மையான பங்குகளை வாங்கியுள்ளது. இந்த முதலீட்டைத் தொடர்ந்து, CoinGecko-வின் வலைத்தளம், GeckoTerminal மற்றும் அதன் மொபைல் செயலி ஆகியவற்றில் Solana-ஆதரவு பெற்ற வர்த்தக வசதிகளை ஒருங்கிணைக்க அறக்கட்டளை திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது.

title: New DeFi-yield generation targets ‘scam-like’ bank accounts that keep all the interest
summary: Crypto native firms like Animoca Brands are betting AI-based agentic commerce to style every area of finance with the so-called “DeFi mullet”
content: Crypto-native firms like Animoca Brands are increasingly leveraging artificial intelligence and agentic commerce to reshape traditional finance. New decentralized finance yield-generation initiatives are targeting traditional bank accounts that retain all the interest, aiming to provide better returns through innovative models often described as the DeFi mullet.
content_ta: Animoca Brands போன்ற கிரிப்டோ நிறுவனங்கள், பாரம்பரிய நிதித்துறையை மாற்றியமைக்க செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு மற்றும் ஏஜென்டிக் காமர்ஸ் தொழில்நுட்பங்களை பயன்படுத்தி வருகின்றன. புதிய DeFi ஈவுத்தொகை திட்டங்கள், அனைத்து வட்டியையும் வைத்துக் கொள்ளும் பாரம்பரிய வங்கி கணக்குகளை இலக்காகக் கொண்டு, புதிய முறைகள் மூலம் சிறந்த லாபத்தை வழங்க முயல்கின்றன.

content: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr has warned that automated AI agents could potentially trigger sudden bank runs in minutes. Speaking at an event in Italy, Barr highlighted that automated financial decisions might overwhelm banks and raised serious concerns regarding AI systems bypassing established security controls.

title: Hackers plant crypto-stealing code on 178 major websites, including HSBC and Ledger

title: Optimizely Hack Hijacked Ledger, BBC and 176 Other Sites to Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses

title: Gate Deepens OpenPayd Partnership to Strengthen Cross-Border Fund and Payment Infrastructure for Gate Money
summary:
Gate, a global crypto and financial services platform with more than 62 million users, has deepened its use of OpenPayd, a leading provider of financial infrastructure, extending its fiat infrastructure across additional entities to support Gate Money, its newly launched all-in-one financial account.
The expansion builds on a relationship dating back to 2022, when Gate first began leveraging OpenPayd’s virtual IBANs to support its European growth through the management and reconciliation of retail and corporate payment flows. Gate is now adding GBP account and EUR SEPA capabilities across a broader range of its operations. These capabilities will support Gate Money while also being available across its wider platform.
Launched on 7 October 2026, Gate Money brings digital assets, equities, payments and asset management into a single unified account. GBP and EUR sit alongside digital assets as core currencies within the product, allowing users to hold, receive, transfer, pay and exchange in one place. The launch marks Gate’s expansion beyond digital asset trading into broader financial services.
Lux Thiagarajah, Chief Commercial Officer at OpenPayd, said: “Gate Money is a major step in Gate’s evolution from a crypto exchange into a broader financial services platform. Bringing assets, accounts and payments together requires fiat infrastructure that can operate across products and markets.



Gate Founder and CEO Dr. Han stated: “Gate Money is a pivotal step in building our one-stop digital financial ecosystem. Expanding our partnership with OpenPayd provides us with robust financial infrastructure to support the seamless integration of our services. Our focus is on simplifying everyday fund management and payments, delivering a truly unified experience that connects multi-asset management for our global users.”
 
NoYesPayments17 Nov, 2026
content: Gate has expanded its partnership with financial infrastructure provider OpenPayd to strengthen cross-border payment capabilities for its newly launched financial account, Gate Money. Building on a relationship that began in 2022, the expanded integration introduces GBP account and EUR SEPA capabilities to support Gate's transition from a digital asset platform into comprehensive financial services, enabling users to seamlessly manage both fiat and digital assets.
content_ta: Gate நிறுவனம் தனது புதிய நிதிக் கணக்கான Gate Money-க்கான எல்லை தாண்டிய கட்டணச் சேவைகளை வலுப்படுத்த நிதி உள்கட்டமைப்பு வழங்குநரான OpenPayd உடனான தனது கூட்டாண்மையை விரிவுபடுத்தியுள்ளது. 2022 ஆம் ஆண்டு தொடங்கிய இந்த உறவின் அடிப்படையில், GBP கணக்கு மற்றும் EUR SEPA வசதிகள் சேர்க்கப்பட்டுள்ளன. இது Gate நிறுவனத்தை ஒரு டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துத் தளத்திலிருந்து விரிவான நிதிச் சேவைகளாக மாற்றவும், பயனர்கள் ஃபியட் மற்றும் டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்களை தடையின்றி நிர்வகிக்கவும் உதவுகிறது.

Luminor’s approach shows how banks can combine proven digital banking technology with their own technology, engineering and market expertise to build experiences around their customers’ needs. This provides a flexible foundation that allows Luminor to continue evolving its digital services as customer expectations change.”

title: 91% of Capital Markets Respondents Want AI to Deliver Greater Accuracy and Fewer Errors
summary:
Broadridge, a global Fintech leader, in collaboration with The ValueExchange, the International Securities Services Association (ISSA), and AI-specialist DeepSee, today released, AI in the Real World 2026: From AI Tools to Controlled Delegation in Post-Trade Operations. The report finds that 91% of respondents want providers to use AI to improve accuracy and reduce operational errors, followed by faster processing (85%), and proactive issue resolutions (80%). The findings put measurable service outcomes, rather than AI adoption alone, at the center of the industry’s next phase of investment.
 
Drawing on more than 200 survey responses and interviews with market participants, the report finds that 61% expect moderate, significant or critical disruption if AI were removed, 78% say no more than one in ten AI use cases operates autonomously. The opportunity is to move from AI to controlled, accountable workflows, with trusted data, clear permissions, and human oversight.
 

“The test of AI is not how many tools a firm deploys, but whether it delivers fewer errors, better client service and increased capacity,” said David Kirby, Head of U.S. Consulting Services, Broadridge. “Achieving those results takes more than a model. Firms need experts who understand post-trade workflows, trusted data and the controls that make AI dependable in production. Broadridge brings that domain expertise together with AI capabilities to help clients target the right opportunities, measure progress and scale with accountability.”
 
The adoption gap in four numbers 
49% report generative AI in production, compared with 11% for agentic AI.
78% say no more than 10% of their AI use cases operate autonomously.
70% describe asset servicing as fully or mostly manual; just 8% say it is fully automated.
80% expect to use AI in external interactions by the end of 2027.
 
Clients want fewer errors and better service
 
Respondents say clients want practical outcomes from AI providers, not technology for its own sake. Improved accuracy and fewer operational errors lead the list (91%), followed by faster processing (85%), better data and reporting (83%), and proactive issue resolution (80%).
 
For firms adopting AI, operational efficiency and cost reduction are the leading objectives, cited by 71% of respondents. The report argues that firms should also measure increased capacity, reduced rework and more consistent service delivery, not cost savings alone. Firms should establish a baseline for errors, rework, turnaround time and capacity, then evaluate AI against those measures. Broadridge combines post-trade expertise, transactional and operational data, and production-ready AI capabilities available through managed services or within clients’ own operations to help firms translate these priorities into practical workflow improvements.
 
The next test: moving AI into core workflows 
 
Application development, client queries, and data quality lead current AI adoption. In asset servicing, 29% of respondents report current AI use and 47% plan to use it, while 70% still describe the process as fully or mostly manual. Settlement, fund accounting, and liquidity management also have more planned than live activity, indicating where firms expect the next wave of implementation.
 
As firms move deeper into core workflows, systems must do more than generate an answer: they must use reliable evidence, act within defined permissions, document their actions, and escalate cases that require human judgment.
 

“The strongest solutions combine AI with process certainty,” said Steve Shillingford, CEO, DeepSee. “In the middle and back office, a wrong answer is a settlement fail or a break someone has to chase. So, a system needs to show the evidence behind a recommendation, act only within its authority, and recognize when to stop and involve a person. When every step is verified against the firm’s own process, AI becomes dependable enough to take on more responsibility. That is the approach we have in production with Broadridge today.” 
 
Controls must keep pace with reliance
 
The research identifies a gap between establishing AI policies and building the assurance needed to expand AI’s role. While 75% of respondents have a responsible-use policy and 65% report defined controls, only 46% report regular audits or explainability requirements, and 24% have processes for building stakeholder trust.
 
The report describes the next stage as “controlled delegation”. AI performs bounded work and takes permitted actions, with clear accountability, monitoring, and escalation. Rather than pursuing autonomy everywhere, firms should expand AI’s authority selectively, based on the risk of each task and demonstrated performance.

title: Uphold Authorized as a Crypto-Asset Service Provider Under the EU's MiCA Regulation
summary:

Authorization requires firms to demonstrate that they meet MiCA’s requirements for the crypto-asset services they provide in the European Economic Area. The Bank of Portugal’s examination analyzed Uphold’s capital and risk safeguards, anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) controls, information security, the segregation and safekeeping of client assets, and the firm’s ownership and governance.

Portugal’s MiCA implementing legislation, Law No. 69/2025, took effect in December 2025 and made the Banco de of Portugal responsible for authorizing crypto-asset service providers, together with Portugal’s securities regulator, the Comissão do Mercado de Valores Mobiliários (CMVM).

The PaysafeGo solution is designed for businesses across industries including travel, retail, gaming, marketplaces, gig economy and creator platforms that are increasingly looking beyond payments acceptance to create deeper, ongoing relationships with their customers. By enabling users to receive, hold, transfer and spend funds within a branded wallet environment, businesses can transform payments from a transactional touchpoint into an engagement and loyalty driver.
"Consumers increasingly expect seamless experiences wherever they engage with brands, and payments are a critical part of that journey," said Bob Legters, Chief Product Officer at Paysafe. "The PaysafeGo wallet solution enables businesses to launch their own branded wallet experience without taking on the burden of licensing, compliance, fraud management, issuing and operational support. By combining the flexibility merchants need with the regulated infrastructure and expertise Paysafe provides, we're helping our partners create stronger customer connections, simplify money movement and unlock new opportunities for growth, so they can spend less time managing payments complexity and more time serving their customers."
The PaysafeGo wallet solution is available through two deployment models designed to accommodate different business requirements.
The Embedded Wallet model enables businesses to integrate a fully branded wallet experience directly into their existing applications and platforms through Paysafe APIs and SDKs. Businesses maintain control over the customer experience and user interface, while Paysafe manages complex backend services including KYC, AML, issuing, settlement, reconciliation, fraud management, compliance, and cross-border payouts.
The Turnkey Wallet model offers a faster path to market through a co-branded wallet experience hosted and managed by Paysafe. In this model, Paysafe manages infrastructure, security, compliance and virtual card issuing, while enabling businesses to maintain a strong branded presence and customer relationship.
Key capabilities of the PaysafeGo wallet solution include real-time payouts, seamless bank and peer-to-peer transfers, branded prepaid cards, customer loyalty and rewards experiences, integrated security and compliance controls, and end-to-end operational support. The solution is designed to help businesses reduce payment and payout costs, eliminate manual operational workflows, increase platform engagement and create new recurring revenue opportunities.

title: Gr4vy Launches Grace, Making Payment Intelligence Accessible Through Conversational AI
summary:
Gr4vy, the cloud-based payment orchestration platform, today announced the launch of Grace, Gr4vy's AI-powered payments intelligence assistant, giving merchants instant visibility into what's driving payment performance across their entire payment ecosystem. Built directly into the Gr4vy platform, Grace helps merchants identify performance gaps, uncover potential revenue opportunities, and assess where changes to their payment strategies could improve results, all through a simple conversation, whether they work with a single payment service provider (PSP) or multiple providers.
Managing payments across multiple providers has given merchants greater flexibility, but it has also made performance harder to assess. Even merchants working with a single PSP face challenges understanding the factors influencing payment performance, from transaction declines and authentication failures to changes in approval rates across markets, payment methods, and customer segments. According to an August 2026 PYMNTS Intelligence report, fragmented payment infrastructure is increasing operational complexity and reducing visibility across payment systems. This challenge was also reflected in feedback from merchants participating in Gr4vy's AI Insights pilot, where the most common request was the ability to ask questions directly about their payment data, highlighting the need for more accessible payment analytics without specialist knowledge or manual reporting.
“Whether a merchant works with one payment provider or several, understanding what's driving payment performance shouldn't require hours of manual analysis,” said John Lunn, Founder and CEO of Gr4vy. “Grace lets anyone on a payments team ask a question in plain language and get an answer they can act on, turning payment data into insights that help businesses make better decisions.”
Grace analyzes payment performance across a merchant's connected PSPs, including authorization rates, declines, payment volumes, refunds, and retry performance. Tasks that previously required navigating several reports, applying filters, or exporting data into spreadsheets can now begin with a single question. Merchants can ask Grace, “Why did my approval rate drop last week?” and get a breakdown of the factors behind the change; compare Visa performance across PSPs and countries; or investigate an individual failed transaction using its transaction ID. For merchants using a single PSP, Grace can help identify patterns in declines, assess performance by payment method or geography, and uncover changes that might otherwise go unnoticed in standard reporting dashboards.
Unlike analytics from individual PSPs, which show performance only within their own systems, Grace lets merchants compare results across all connected PSPs using consistent metrics. It can also assess the effectiveness of payment retries and compare performance before and after changes to routing rules. For example, Grace can show how often declined payments succeed on subsequent retries and compare how each PSP performs on those attempts, helping merchants identify opportunities to optimize their retry strategies and improve approval rates.
Merchants can explore these findings further through follow-up questions without rebuilding reports or applying new filters. Responses include written explanations supported by tables and charts showing trends, comparisons, and breakdowns of what has changed.
Designed to operate within Gr4vy's secure payment infrastructure, Grace acts as a payments analyst whose findings merchants can verify. It combines AI with tested payment calculations rather than relying on AI-generated figures. The assistant only accesses information permitted to the signed-in user, respecting existing user permissions and access controls. Merchant data is never used to train AI models, and Grace operates in an advisory capacity, providing analysis and recommendations without making changes to merchants' payment configurations.
By making payment analytics accessible through natural-language questions, Grace enables finance, operations, product, and customer support teams to investigate performance without specialist analytics knowledge. It also explains payment terminology, including decline codes and authentication processes, helping teams understand their findings and make more informed decisions.
The launch builds on Gr4vy's broader payment orchestration strategy. While its platform gives merchants control over how payments are routed, Grace helps them understand where to use that control to improve performance. Grace is available through the Gr4vy Dashboard, where merchants can access the assistant using their existing login credentials.

title: Stitch Launches Stitch AI, Bringing Agentic AI Directly Into Banking Operations
summary:
Stitch today announced the launch of Stitch AI, bringing  agentic AI directly into the operating system for banks and financial institutions. Natively, built into the Stitch operating system, financial institutions can deploy agents within existing governance and approval controls. The launch is accompanied with “Anyone can be a hero,” a campaign film starring Hollywood actor Patrick J. Adams which can be viewed on stitch.co/ai. Stitch AI gives financial institutions three ways to put AI to work.
Copilot:. Bank staff ask it to fetch data, execute a task or change a configuration in plain language. It pulls data on accounts and customers, sets up products from accounts and cards to loans, including limits, pricing, fees and eligibility, and updates workflows.
Stitch Agents:  Ready-made AI agents handle everyday banking operations, including onboarding, credit decisioning and collections. They operate within the bank's existing workflows, permissions and rules.
Agent Harness: An enterprise-grade framework that allows banks to build, configure, test and deploy their own AI agents, with permissions, approvals, guardrails and audit trails built in.
All three operate within the limits the bank sets. Above them, they ask.
Most AI in banking is added on top of legacy systems, where data sits in places that were never designed to work together.  Legacy tools work on incomplete copies of records, with no direct access to accounts or customers. They can answer questions but cannot execute tasks, enforce approvals or operate within the controls required by regulated financial institutions. Customer data may also pass through external systems beyond the bank's direct oversight.
Stitch AI is built into the operating system. Agents act on the core system itself, through the same services the bank’s products already run on, with no copies of data and no separate connectors to maintain. Every agent has its own identity, scoped permissions, hard limits, maker-checker, a full audit trail, and every control a regulated institution expects. Sensitive data, including ID numbers, account numbers, phone numbers and addresses, is masked before any model sees it. Every question, action and approval is logged with the reasoning behind it, so risk and compliance teams have a complete record of what happened and who signed it off.
Banks decide where Stitch AI runs and which model it uses. It deploys in-country or in a private cloud, on your model of choice, and banks can switch models without rebuilding anything while remaining in full control of their data
“Most AI projects in banks gets stuck at the proof of concept because the systems underneath can’t accept them and in this regulated industry, nobody lets an agent act without an owner and an approval. Stitch solves both. We make modernising easy, and AI comes built into the operating system, under the bank’s controls, from day one.” said Mohamed Oueida, CEO of Stitch.

title: Sumsub Identity Fraud Report: U.S. Has World’s Largest Fraud Network Detected as AI Agents Open New Gaps
summary:
Sumsub, the first AI-powered trust infrastructure, today released its sixth annual Identity Fraud Report, which found that the largest single fraud network Sumsub detected in any country was in the U.S., linking 3,173 users. U.S. fraud is shifting from individual bad actors to the networks behind them with increased complexity despite the U.S. fraud rate on Sumsub's platform dropping 45% year-over-year.
The Sumsub Fraud Complexity Index (FCI) debuts as a proprietary measure of how sophisticated confirmed fraud has become. Globally, the fraud rate fell for a second consecutive year to 1.6%, but the FCI rose in every region Sumsub analyzed. This signals that fraud is becoming less frequent but harder to stop amid the growing use of generative AI, including deepfakes which rose 31%.
Fraud is shifting from individuals to networks
According to the report, 1 in 3 businesses (33%) that experienced fraud said at least 25% of their confirmed cases were linked to a wider network of accounts, devices or payment instruments, some of which form after an account passes verification and is sold or taken over. However, only 16% of U.S. and Canadian businesses use fraud network analysis. 
"Fraud teams are built to catch the one bad transaction or the one bad account, and they're very good at it," said Erin West, former deputy district attorney and founder of Operation Shamrock. "A scam network is designed to look like a thousand ordinary people doing ordinary things. Every account is verified, and every document is real, because the person holding it was recruited, paid, or coerced into opening it, so nothing trips a wire on its own."
Lack of AI agent visibility reveals confidence gap
A year after Sumsub warned that agentic AI scams were poised to surge, 53% of businesses globally said they had detected or suspected fraud involving an AI agent. In nearly half of those cases (49%), a legitimate agent had been manipulated by malicious instructions, and in 30%, an agent initiated a purchase, payment or transfer. U.S. and Canadian businesses are confident but underprepared: 84% feel fairly or very protected against fraud, yet fewer than 1 in 3 (29%) verify who authorizes an AI agent, and fewer than 1 in 10 (9%) can suspend one. 
With the proliferation of AI agents accelerating, blanket restrictions face challenges without defined parameters for what agents are permitted to do. The findings come as major U.S. banks restrict third-party AI agents from customer accounts, and weeks after OpenAI disclosed that one of its research agents spent crypto funds without permission. Sumsub's recently expanded Know Your Agent framework links each agent to a verified human and requires a human check when an agent tries to exceed its permissions.
Money is taken, not handed over
When U.S. and Canadian consumers experience fraud exposure, it is more often taken than handed over. 43% of victims had money taken from an account or card without permission, compared with 23% who were tricked into paying. Only 21% of U.S. and Canadian businesses use transaction monitoring. Americans reported a record $15.9 billion in fraud losses to the Federal Trade Commission in 2025.
"North America may have a lower fraud rate than the other regions in our data, but the scale of the market means the absolute impact can still be enormous," said Danielle Labarbera, vice president of sales for the U.S. at Sumsub. "In the U.S. especially, fraud and improper payments involving public money have become a much bigger government priority, and we're seeing more attention on how these losses can be prevented earlier. At the same time, some of the largest fraud networks we detect are here. The remaining risk can be highly concentrated and very expensive when it gets through."
Lawmakers are responding
While the regulatory frameworks and technical infrastructure exist, timely coordination between businesses and policymakers is necessary to effectively combat emerging threats. The SCAM Act, which would require platforms that sell ads to verify advertisers and guard against false, stolen or synthetic identities, has gained 10 Senate sponsors from both parties since February but remains in committee. Kids' online safety legislation could still move in the lame-duck session. The House passed its KIDS Act package in June, and the Senate's Kids Online Safety Act, backed by 76 co-sponsors, awaits a floor vote after an attempt to fast-track it was blocked in September. In Canada, Bill C-277, the proposed Regulating the Online Use of Deepfakes Act, would require platforms to detect, label and remove harmful deepfakes, including those causing financial damage or identity theft.

title: Approval Rate Field Guide From Ecommpay and Corefy Helps Merchants Improve Checkout Performance

The new Approval Rate Field Guide provides actionable insights to direct merchants in fully understanding their approval rates, diagnosing the causes of declines and building a recovery layer to recapture lost volume.
The approval rate is simply the percentage of submitted transactions that are approved by the issuing bank or acquirer. While this is an important metric to help track payment performance, and the primary KPI for most payment teams, the formula covers just one element of a longer journey which contains many stages where a transaction could fail. In this guide, we show merchants what to look for and how to make changes that will improve overall checkout performance.”
Ecommpay is committed to helping merchants increase transaction success, and sharing the Approval Rate Field Guide forms an important part of that mission. Payments teams must do more than monitor their approval rate to meaningfully improve checkout performance, they need to own it; segmenting the data to understand what is driving declines. Working with suitable tools and  providers can give merchants infrastructure to help recapture lost transactions and support revenue growth, although results will vary between merchants.
